findings.claim: EXHAUSTION is a retirement that is not a test, and real edges get retired far more often than the goal's 15%. Section 3 retires 'for good' every learning version whose run has not passed by its 60th block. I ran the chosen rule on the judge's own power arrays with search_judge.first_pass (check1/exhaustion_c1.py, output exhaustion_c1.out). A true 60 bp edge at rho_day 0.05 gets retired by exhaustion 26% / 37% / 56% / 60% / 71% of the time at 85 / 30 / 13 / 8 / 3 events a session (120-session cells for 13, 8 and 3). At rho_day 0.15 it is 48% / 55% / 65% / 65% / 80%. A true 100 bp edge is retired 1-44% (0.05) and 15-51% (0.15). The lower-tail RETIRE adds only 0.3-1.7%. The goal makes retirement a sequential test at FP <= 15%. Section 4.4's 'at most 0.9% of 60 bp programs within 60' counts only the lower tail and leaves exhaustion out.
findings.fix: Replace section 2's HORIZON paragraph and section 3's RETIREMENT item 2 with: 'EXHAUSTION ends the RUN, not the version. At the close at which the run's 60th block is covered, a version in learning whose run has not passed stays in learning (real money at learning size continues). RUN n+1 starts with the next block and is tested by sections 1.2-2 on its own record, with its own looks and seed strings "run{n+1}|". It is charged FALSE_PASS_RATE_6 against the lane's count when it starts, as a fresh run after a demotion is. Only section 1.4's RETIRE, the lower tail, retires.' Code: bands.on_evl6 must not move a version to retired on look.test.exhausted; _run_evl6 advances the test ordinal m instead. In 4.4, report the real-edge retirement rate split by mechanism: the lower tail at 0.3-1.7%, and runs ended.

findings.claim: The demotion fixed reads demote a real edge more than 15% of the time, and the rule's wording is ambiguous. judge/demotion_check.py modelled each session's six Probe events with only a 1% market move. It left out the residual day shock that the promotion calibration itself uses. check1/demotion_c1.py adds it: sd_c from rho_day, AR 0.10 t(3), the volatility regime, sigma_i 1-10% t(3), +-30% jumps, 20,000 paths. With it, the cumulative-mean reads (mean r < 0 at the 100th, 200th ... Probe+ event) demote a real 60 bp edge 15-20% of the time at rho_day 0.05 and 20-29% at 0.15, by the 100th to 1000th event (16-21% and 21-29% with a 20 bp drift). At rho_day 0 they reproduce the draft's 12-15%. Even the draft's own 16.2% at 500 events is above 15%, and the goal makes demotion a test at FP <= 15%. The text also leaves three things open: whether 'those events' means all the stay's events (the check computed cumulative) or the last 100; whether r is fill-based or the shadow's; and the order of events that settle at the same close.
findings.fix: Section 3 DEMOTION 3 should read: 'At the stay's 100th, 200th, ... settled real-money event at Probe size or above, demote when the one-sided session-block sign-flip p for a mean BELOW zero, over ALL the stay's real-money Probe+ events so far, is <= 0.20. Events are ordered by scheduled exit close, then entry decision time, then event id. Block = entry session; value = the mean of its events' fill-based after-fee r. Exact for <= 16 blocks, else 99,999 vectors with seed string f"{id}|v{version}|evl6|stay{n}|read{k}".' Measured in check1/demotion_c1b.py (self-normalized normal approximation): it demotes a real 60 bp edge 4.7% (rho 0.05) or 7.7% (rho 0.15) within 1000 events. It demotes a zero-edge program 33-47% of the time by the 300th-1000th event, and a cost-only -15 bp program 46-67%. Add to section 3 that demotion's FP means P(demoting a true 60 bp edge, all three triggers together) at the worst plausible cell, and report that figure. Also update PREREG-EVL-4's cost of a false pass, which assumed 'a Probe stay of about 100 events': a false pass now stays at Probe longer.

findings.claim: The claimed FP is not established once re-measured on fresh paths, and day-shock momentum, which no outcome-free data can measure, is fixed at one value. The 0.131 worst figure was measured on the same paths that chose this rule out of 2,457. I re-ran calib_judge.py's generator unchanged with fresh seeds (check1/calib_c1.py, run_c1.py, run_c1e.py; 4,000 programs). The judge's own worst cell (crash days, left-skewed events, a 20 bp AR 0.97 drift, rho 0.15, 85 a session) passes 0.141 and 0.140 of the time. Pooled, that is 0.1405 +- 0.0055, with a one-sided 95% upper bound of about 0.150, not 2.5 SE under 15%. Section 4.3 sets day-shock momentum to AR 0.10 in every plausible cell and gives no reason why 0.10 is the ceiling. At AR 0.20 the same corner gives 0.156 +- 0.008 (lag 0 and lag 3); at 0.25 it gives 0.166-0.178. Two checks it survived: a drift of persistence AR 0.70-0.90 held to the judge's own yardstick of +-3.8% a month (0.127-0.144), and event counts coupled to the day shock, with the knife edge set on money weights (0.087-0.128). Section 4.4's fallback, 0.012/0.003, also has a flaw: a pass at block 6 becomes impossible (2^-6 = 0.0156 > 0.012), which contradicts section 2's 6-block minimum.
findings.fix: Use alpha(S) = 0.016 for 6 <= S <= 9, 0.012 for 10 <= S <= 20 and 0.003 for 21 <= S <= 60. The margin, looks, minimums and guards stay as they are. On the judge's grid (check1/judge_grid_pw.out): worst plausible 0.118 (lag 0) / 0.119 (lag 3), base 0.041-0.043. On the fresh-seed corner: 0.129/0.121 and 0.128/0.124. At momentum AR 0.20: 0.140/0.141. With drift persistence 0.70-0.90 at +-3.8% a month: at most 0.132. Power at 60 bp by session 10/20/40: 0.156 / 0.302 / 0.377, against the chosen rule's 0.167 / 0.332 / 0.405 and PREREG-EVL-3's 0.290 by session 20. At 100 bp by session 20: 0.584 against 0.612. The first possible pass stays at block 6. Then: make momentum up to AR 0.20 part of 4.3's plausible grid and report AR 0.25 as a stress; report the fresh-seed replicates in 4.4; set FALSE_PASS_RATE_6 = 0.13; and change code_plan's evl6_alpha to these three pieces. If the captain keeps 0.016/0.004 anyway, the record must say 0.140 +- 0.0055 at the corner and 0.156 at momentum AR 0.20, not 0.131.

findings.claim: The test's estimand is not stated. The sign-flip tests the session-weighted block mean. The 'mean a > 0' guard, and Done's per-event bound, use the event-weighted mean. Real money weights a session by min(n_s, 6), because Probe holds at most 6 positions. I let event counts rise with the size of the day shock: count x exp(0.3 min(|eps|, 4)), about 2x on a crash day (calib_c1.py cnt_kappa, ew_knife). A program whose event-weighted mean a is exactly 0 then passes 0.12-0.35 of the time at 3-30 events a session and rho 0.15 (eval_c1.all.out, B rows). Its block mean is +30 bp, and at <= 6 positions a session it does earn that. With the knife edge set on money weights (calib_c1m.py), the FP is 0.087-0.128 (eval_c1.M.out).
findings.fix: Add to 1.2: 'The null this screen rejects is the money-weighted mean after-cost a, sessions weighted by min(n_s, the band's open cap). The event-weighted mean is reported beside. The claim holds while learning, Probe and Sized cap open positions per session.' No rule change is needed.

findings.claim: The new versions' record before the release can be built two ways. Section 1.1 says each new version 'takes its superseded version's events ... word for word'. code_plan item 4 instead decides the new rows 'BY THEMSELVES as a backfill' (decide-open-evl6 / decide-close-evl6). The two give different records. Under re-decision, a new version has no holdings before REGISTERED_AT_6, so it can take issuers that the superseded version's 5-session cooldown skipped. The backfill rule (status=all, news edited more than 10 minutes after publication dropped, late-stored rows taken) also differs from the live decisions the superseded version made in those sessions.
findings.fix: Add to 1.1: 'For every session decided before the House release carrying this file, a new version's intents are exactly its superseded version's intents for that session, keeping those whose events are knowable after REGISTERED_AT_6, with the same skips, cooldown and live or backfill rule as decided at the time. From the release on it is decided by itself, and its 5-session cooldown counts the superseded version's holdings.' In code_plan item 4, copy the superseded rows' intents rather than re-deciding.

findings.claim: Raising the lane's lifetime budget from 3.0 to 4.2 expected false passes is called a 'restatement on the same basis'. In the budget's own unit, which is what PREREG-EVL-4 section 3 stated and priced, it is a 40% relaxation; only the seat count stays the same. The run fix above (each fresh run charged) and the alpha fix (0.13) also change the arithmetic.
findings.fix: In section 5, call it a relaxation the captain accepts by amendment and give the reason (the same thirty seats, re-measured). Restate the budget at 0.13 a version or run: 30 x 0.13 = 3.9, with 15 x 0.13 = 1.95 used at registration plus births. Alternatively keep 3.0, which allows 23 versions or runs.

findings.claim: Some wording a coder could read two ways. In 1.4 and RETIRE, 'its mean a > 0 and its mean r > 0' and 'the record's mean a < 0' do not say whether they are event-weighted or block-weighted. Today's screen.look_figures and the judge's simulation both use event-weighted means over TRADABLE events. Section 3's 'entering after that move' does not say whether the events of the first Probe decision belong to the stay record.
findings.fix: Write: 'mean a and mean r are means over the record's TRADABLE events (event-weighted, math.fsum)'. Write: 'a stay record holds the version's TRADABLE events whose entry decision is at or after the first decision made at Probe'.

findings.claim: The provenance line says the registering captain 'took no part in designing, calibrating or choosing these rules'. The captain session (6e6a85b9) wrote this workflow and every prompt, including the prompt for this check. It also makes the replace-versus-keep decision after having read the Oct 19-20 per-program shadow means. Discarding the events of Oct 19-21 is a choice the captain makes knowing those outcomes.
findings.fix: Cite the sha256 of workflow wf_560ee5dd-ef8's script and state that its prompts carry only outcome-free counts (evl5/HOUSE-FACTS.json, evl4/FACTS.json). Record in the registering amendment that the replacement follows the blind judge's FP finding (the union at 0.199 is over 0.15, and PREREG-EVL-3 alone is at 0.152), that it applies to every program alike, and that the captain used no discretion per program.

findings.claim: The 13.1% worst plausible holds up on fresh seeds, but it only holds because day-shock persistence is fixed at one value. Fresh seeds at the corner (crash days, left-skewed events, 20 bp drift at AR 0.97, rho_day 0.15, 85 events a session) give 0.129 +-0.003 over 11,000 programs, against the judge's 0.131. So the 2,457-rule search left no winner's curse. However, the grid holds the residual day shock's AR at 0.10 'always', and the draft gives no argument for 0.10 as a ceiling (calib_strata itself went to 0.40). With crash days, the false-positive rate climbs steeply with that AR. At the corner: phi 0.15 gives 0.133; phi 0.20 gives 0.163 +-0.004 at 85 a session (0.159 at 30); phi 0.25 gives 0.183 +-0.004 at 85 (0.167 at 30, 0.149 at 8). Crash days alone at phi 0.25 (no drift, symmetric events) give 0.159. A 15 bp drift tied to the volatility regime, added at the corner, gives 0.156. With symmetric days, phi 0.25 stays at 0.10-0.12, so the break is persistence combined with left-skewed days. About half the rate is spent at blocks 6-10 (7-13 points), where no persistence can be measured. The S=6 look alone is a pure sign test (all six blocks above 10 bp) and costs 2.3-5.8 points. Stresses, for the record: crash days at 10% of sessions at -2.5 sd give 0.189; AR 0.99 drift stays under the cap (0.144 / 0.134). PREREG-EVL-3 alone is worse (0.199 at phi 0.25, 30 a session), so replacing it is still right; the chosen constants are what fail. Runs: evl6/check2/run1, run3, run5, run6, run7 .jsonl.
findings.fix:
Put phi_day 0.15 and 0.20 at rho_day <= 0.15 into the plausible grid, in every shape and drift, and name 0.25 as a stress. Then freeze a rule that holds there on fresh seeds. Two exact candidates from my runs, both keeping the 20 looks' list, the 10 bp margin and the guards:
(a) The speed-keeping rule. Drop the S=6 look, so looks start at block 7. Set alpha(S) = 0.016 for S 7-10, 0.010 for S 11-20 and 0.003 for S 21-60. Results: 0.141 at the phi 0.20 corner, 0.108 worst on the judge's own grid, 0.038 base. P(60 bp promoted by session 8/10/20/40), mean over the five rates: 0.107/0.158/0.281/0.365, against 0.119/0.167/0.332/0.405 today. Lag-3 by session 10: 0.078 against 0.096.
(b) The draft's own section 4.4 fallback: alpha 0.012 for S <= 20 and 0.003 after. Results: 0.135 at phi 0.20, 0.151 at phi 0.25, by session 10/20/40 0.127/0.287/0.366.
Either way, the first possible pass moves to block 7: the Oct 30 close for O1 rows, Oct 31 for close-entry rows. Restate sections 0, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6 and 5 on the widened grid; the 0.14 charge still covers it. If phi 0.25 at the corner must also stay under 15%, both rules sit at 15-16%; you would need alpha 0.012/0.004 with a 15 bp margin (0.137) or a 20 bp margin (0.128), which are slower.

findings.claim: The test and its money condition read a different population from the one the money buys. At Probe, real money holds at most 6 positions a program (8 at learning), chosen by the program's ranking: verdict score, then ADV highest first, or the reaction for REACT rows. Most seats run 20-165 events a session, so at 85 a session money buys about 7% of the events: the highest-scored, most liquid names. The screen, its margin, and its 'mean a > 0, mean r > 0' condition all average every TRADABLE shadow event. A program whose edge sits in its lower-ranked, illiquid names (where Lopez-Lira and Tang, and Berkman et al., put the effect) has no edge in what it buys. It still passes at the test's power, not at 13%: by the draft's own section 4.5, a 30 bp all-event edge passes 0.24 within 60 sessions at 85 a session, and a 60 bp edge 0.74. So the owner's 'a promoted program must have a positive mean after-cost a' is never checked on what real money buys.
findings.fix: Add a PASS guard in section 1.4, computed from the same record. In each block, take the top-K TRADABLE events by the program's own ranking: intents.rank_key descending, then ADV descending, before ROOM and the sale gate, with K = 6 (the Probe cap). The mean a of those events over the record must be > 0, and the event-weighted mean r > 0. For a block with 6 or fewer events this is the existing condition. Write it with every look. It can only lower the false-positive rate. Measure its power cost in the recalibration; it should be small when the ranking is uninformative, because the top-K and the full block share the day shock.

findings.claim: At low rates, the equal block weights are not the money's weights. With 6 or fewer events a session, money holds one position per event, so its null is the event-weighted mean; the test weights blocks equally. The generator draws counts independently of returns. Try a coupling where a session at twice its normal event intensity carries a lower residual (kappa = 1% or 2%; corr about -0.25 / -0.46 at rho_day 0.15). Then the block mean is +kappa/3 while the per-event mean is 0. At 3 events a session the false-positive rate rises from 0.050 to 0.094 (kappa 1%) and to 0.151 (kappa 2%). The event-weighted guard never binds: mean a > 0, and even > 10 bp, gives the identical rate. At 8 or more a session the cap makes money nearly block-weighted, so passes there are real money edges (+22 to +32 bp), not false passes. Runs: evl6/check2/run1.jsonl and run4b.jsonl.
findings.fix: Use y_s = min(n_s, 6) x (B_s - 0.0010) as the sign-flip values, where n_s is the block's TRADABLE count. This is the money a Probe session can hold, and it equals the draft's x_s whenever a session has 6 or more events. Results: 0.096 falls to 0.068, 0.151 to 0.086, the corner at 3 / 8 a session from 0.111 / 0.117 to 0.105 / 0.113. Power at 60 bp by session 60 is unchanged (3 a session 0.255 to 0.240; 8 a session 0.356 to 0.358). Include it in the recalibration.

findings.claim: Section 0's premise is overstated. On 4,000 fresh programs, PREREG-EVL-3 alone scores 0.143 +-0.0055 at the judge's own worst cell (crash days, 20 bp, rho_day 0.15, 30 a session), against 0.152 +-0.008. The 15.2% is the maximum over about 90 noisy cells, so 'already at the cap' is not established. The case for replacing it still holds for other reasons: the union reaches about 0.20, PREREG-EVL-3 alone reaches 0.199 at phi 0.25, and it is never better than the new rule in any cell.
findings.fix: Restate section 0 and section 4.4 as '14.3-15.2% on two seed sets; 0.199 at phi_day 0.25'. Rest A91's override on the union and on the widened grid, not on 15.2% alone.

findings.claim: The draft cites a superseded goal. The owner re-set it on Oct 21 (goal-2026-10-19/GOAL-MESSAGE-V3.txt), and V3's Done needs the 95% issuer-block lower bound above zero 'raw and net of each event's benchmark'. The draft cites V2, and section 6 restates Done word for word from PREREG-EVL-3 section 5, with only the raw-return bound. A coder reading this file would build the weaker Done.
findings.fix: Cite GOAL-MESSAGE-V3.txt in the header. In section 6, either restate Done as V3 words it (both the raw r and the abnormal a lower bounds above zero), or point to the current Done reader instead of restating it.

findings.claim: Section 1.4 contradicts section 1.3 on the tolerance. Section 1.4 writes PASS as 'p <= alpha(S) + 1e-12'. Section 1.3 says 'every comparison carries the 1e-12 tolerance in the program's disfavour', which for PASS means alpha - 1e-12. screen.judge_look today uses p <= alpha with no tolerance. For S >= 17 a Monte Carlo p can equal 0.016 or 0.004 exactly (1,600 or 400 out of 100,000), so the readings differ.
findings.fix: PASS when p <= alpha(S), with no tolerance, as screen.py does. RETIRE and the stay's demotion when q <= alpha(S) + 1e-12. Make section 1.3's general sentence name only the sums.

findings.claim:
Four rules can be coded two ways.
(a) The fixed reads take 'the mean after-cost r of those events'. That could be cumulative over the stay (what judge/demotion_check.py computes, giving the 13-16%) or the last 100.
(b) The money stop is 'the stay's last 50' but is labelled 'PREREG-EVL-3 section 2, unchanged', and PREREG-EVL-3's stop is not stay-limited. It is also silent on a stay with fewer than 50 events.
(c) Seed tags: '"" for the first run, "run{n}|" for its n-th run' leaves open whether the first run is "run1|".
(d) It does not say whether a fresh run after demotion needs room in the lane budget before it starts.
findings.fix:
Pin each:
(a) Cumulative over all of the stay's settled real-money events at Probe size or above.
(b) Stay-limited, with 'all of them when fewer than 50', and drop 'unchanged'.
(c) Tags "" for run 1, "run{n}|" for n >= 2, "stay{n}|" for n >= 1.
(d) A fresh run starts whatever the budget and is charged 0.14 when it starts.

findings.claim: Section 1.1 says each new version takes its superseded version's events 'word for word', but the code does not do that for about five sessions. One position per issuer (programs._held_recently, plus A72) is keyed on (program, version). A version that starts empty at REGISTERED_AT_6 will take issuers the superseded version holds, or held in the last 5 sessions.
findings.fix: Say that the new version's one-position-per-issuer is computed over its own intents from REGISTERED_AT_6 on, so its record may differ for the first five sessions. Alternatively, require it over both versions' intents. Choose before the first look.

findings.claim: A late release gives the captain an option that depends on outcomes. If the release misses the Oct 28 close, 'every PREREG-EVL-3 look held before the release stands with the move it made'. The registering captain reads the lane's records and controls when the release lands, so it could see a superseded version heading for an Oct 28 pass and let it happen.
findings.fix: In the registering amendment, make the superseded versions non-promoting from REGISTERED_AT_6 whatever the release date. Their PREREG-EVL-3 looks are still written but move no band: a one-line bands.on_look guard shipped first, or a seat kill. Then no test choice depends on timing.

findings.claim: Exhaustion is a retirement without a test. The goal lists retirement among the pre-registered tests at <= 15%, but exhaustion retires every learning version unpassed at block 60. A real 60 bp edge is retired 26% (85 a session) to 65% (8 a session) to about 75% (3 a session) of the time; a 100 bp edge 1-49% (from section 4.5). Coming back needs a new version, which slows iteration.
findings.fix: Report the false-retirement rate beside section 4.5. Rename the outcome 'end of run', not retirement. Pre-register an automatic next version of the same spec at that close, charged 0.14 when the budget allows, with no new file. Or state the departure from the goal's words in the amendment.

findings.claim: Section 2 overclaims, and the issuer-block test is quietly demoted. Section 2 says the session-block sign-flip 'holds its level whatever the shock's size, its loading...'. That is true only for blocks that are independent and symmetric; the skew, drift and persistence measured in section 4 are why the rule gives 13% and not its nominal level. Separately, the goal says <= 15% 'by issuer-block permutation'. PREREG-EVL-1 and -3 held the issuer-block test at the screen's alpha (0.018, with its skew check); this draft makes it a 0.10 guard.
findings.fix: Reword section 2 to state the conditions and point to section 4 for the departures. Record in the amendment that the false-positive rate is carried by the session-block test and that the goal's issuer-block permutation is a 0.10 guard, so the owner sees this reading.
